rationale: No suitable evidence-supported optimization fits this release workflow without weakening coverage or violating stated contraindications. The workflow is a release/deployment workflow (triggered on release published and workflow_dispatch) that builds wheels across multiple platforms and publishes to PyPI/TestPyPI. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is contraindicated because every matrix/platform outcome is required for a complete release, and canceling remaining jobs would hide required build results. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is explicitly contraindicated for release or deployment work. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency download caching) is already partially addressed: Rust compilation uses sccache via maturin-action, and there is no explicit pip install step or pyproject.toml-driven dependency installation in this workflow to which a pip cache could attach; the measured pip-cache evidence comes from a test workflow with `pip install '.[dev]'` and `pytest`, which does not match this release workflow. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks representative successful-duration history (CI history shows only a single cancelled run), so a safe timeout cannot be derived. Adding unrelated caching or timeout steps would not preserve intended behavior and is not supported by the available evidence.
